title: Plus/Dot Username Normalization — scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes about how we handle usernames that contain "+" (plus-addressing) and "." (periods/dots) in the user identifier fields (email- or username-like inputs). This is a scratchpad for edge cases to include in the cleanup pipeline and for labeling guidance for the microlabeler team.

Context / why: 
- We see many near-duplicate accounts where the only difference is "+tag" or extra dots.
- Some downstream features (auth join, dedupe, recommendations) assume canonical identity; incorrect normalization causes duplicate users, bad telemetry attribution, and eval noise.
- We need consistent, safety-conscious rules so that human labelers and automated cleansers behave predictably.

Observed patterns and examples (real-ish samples scrubbed):
- alice.smith@example.com vs alicesmith@example.com (dots removed)
- bob+newsletter@provider.co vs bob@provider.co (plus alias)
- joao.silva+promo@pt.example vs joao.silva@pt.example (Portuguese domain, accents elsewhere)
- x.y+z@sub.mail.example vs x.y@sub.mail.example (subdomain present)
- user.name%company@domain (percent-encoded local-part)
- CAPITALNAME+tag@domain.COM vs capitalname@domain.com (case differences)
- trailing dot in local-part weirdness: "local."@example (rare, quoted)
- unicode dots: user·name@domain (middle dot) and fullwidth dot variants

High-level heuristics (draft):
1) Domain canonicalization: always lowercase domain, strip display-name whitespace. Keep punycode conversion for IDNA domains.
2) Local-part canonicalization: default = no change. Only apply transformations when downstream benefit is clear and when we can map to verified behavior for provider.
3) Provider-aware rules: if domain is in PROVIDERS_PLUS_ALIAS set (gmail, googlemail, fastmail-like) then strip plus tags. Else keep plus parts and surface to labelers.
4) Dots: only remove dots for domains known to ignore them (gmail/googlemail). For unknown domains, do NOT remove by default; instead mark as candidate duplicate for adjudication.
5) Case sensitivity: local-part case is technically sensitive for some mail servers; canonicalize to lowercase for widely-used providers (gmail, outlook?). Mark as "case-normalized" in metadata.

Labeler guidance (short):
- If labeler recognizes the provider as one that normalizes plus/dots (common list provided), tag as "alias" and choose canonical (strip plus/dots).
- If unknown provider and ambiguous: choose "leave" and add reason e.g., "unknown-provider-dot-risk".
- For accounts with quotes/escaped chars ("local."@domain) mark as "weird-quoted-local" and escalate if critical for product mapping.
- For Unicode or homoglyph dots/characters, flag as "possible-homoglyph" and sample for fraud team if repeated pattern.

Edge-case decision table (for implementers / labelers):
- local-part contains "+":
  - domain in PLUS_SAFE_LIST => normalize (strip plus and everything after)
  - else => do not normalize; label tag-preserve + includes original plus text in metadata
- local-part contains ".":
  - domain in DOT_SAFE_LIST => remove dots and collapse
  - else => keep as-is and add "dot-ambiguous" to notes
- local-part has percent/encoded sequences: decode if domain known to present that pattern else pass-through
- quoted local-parts (contains double quotes ") => preserve exactly; do not apply simple dot or plus rules

Suggested small safe default pipeline (for nightly cleansing job):
1) Trim whitespace, lowercase domain, normalize unicode domain via IDNA.
2) If domain in PLUS_SAFE_LIST: strip "+" and trailing token, record original in metadata.original_local
3) If domain in DOT_SAFE_LIST: remove dots in local-part, record mapping
4) Apply dedupe lookup using canonicalized email; if collision, push to adjudication queue with reason codes
5) For unknown domains, submit as candidate to human-review sampling (rate-limited)

Test cases to add to unit tests (quick):
- alice.smith+promo@gmail.com -> alicesmith@gmail.com (PASS)
- user.name@smallhost.test -> user.name@smallhost.test (no change)
- "local."@example.com -> "local."@example.com (preserve)
- João.Silva+news@exemplo.pt -> joao.silva@exemplo.pt OR depending on provider rules (normalize accents?) -> ACTION: do not fold accents automatically; IDN domain conversion only
- Percent encoded: joe%2Bhome@service.com -> treat as literal percent or decode? -> record and vote to decode for known-safe providers

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which domains beyond gmail/fastmail should be in PLUS_SAFE_LIST? (ask SRE/auth team for provider behavior list)
- Do we canonicalize accents on local-part? Risky -> avoid unless provider doc states so.
- How to represent metadata from normalization steps in our events/DB so we can revert for audits? Need schema for normalization_history (simple list of strings).
- Need to add a small adjudication UI column: "canonical suggestion" + "confidence" + "reason". Wire to microlabeler.
- Create a small sample set (200 rows) with varied patterns for labeler training. Balance by frequency and risk.

Implementation notes / quick snippets for devs: (pseudo-friendly)
- PROVIDERS_PLUS_ALIAS = ["gmail.com", "googlemail.com", "fastmail.com"] (-> maintainable config)
- PROVIDERS_DOT_IGNORE = ["gmail.com", "googlemail.com"]
- store: {original, normalized, rules_applied: ["strip-plus","lowercase-domain"], actor: "auto\/human"}
- ensure we never drop original raw string; always keep raw_local and raw_domain fields

Sample adjudication labels (for microlabeler):
- keep-as-is
- normalize-strip-plus
- normalize-remove-dots
- preserve-quoted-local
- possible-fraud-homoglyph
- escalate-auth-team

Quick notes from Slack and PRs: 
- Samir: "for fastmail, plus works differently depending on mailbox type" (see slack thread TS#3421)
- GH PR 128 contains earlier dot-safe list and tests — need to reconcile with new provider list

Next steps (for me):
- build 200-row sample, push to GH gist, link to labeling batch (LABEL-482).
- sync with auth/SRE next Tuesday re: provider canonicalization behavior.
- propose minimal schema for normalization_history and show in microlabeler UI as a short badge.

Notes to self: keep rules narrow and reversible. Prefer human-in-the-loop for unknown domains. Avoid aggressive normalizations that might mask distinct recipients (esp for enterprise hosts).

-- end scratchpad --

References and quick links: 
- Confluence (placeholder): CONFLUE-identity-normalization
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/labeling/pull/128
- JIRA: LABEL-482
